doc.title: Roy Haynes — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Playing Monk's music and Evidence
summary: Monk's odd tempos were a challenge and he would come in on drum solos; Griffin kept saying he had it.

story.theme_name: Charlie Parker, Dizzy and the bebop revolution
story.community_name: Playing with and understanding Thelonious Monk

blocks.x: You like Monk’s music? I love the way you play on Evidence.
On Evidence? I did the [?] of that. Oh, boy.

Monk’s – it was really a challenge. He used to say, he says, “Drummers can only play at three tempos.” He know that his … was odd tempos and odd – sometime you didn’t know what to – you had to make something to play on it.
Was he like all the other great leaders you worked for, just let you do what you want to do? Or did he suggest anything?
Even if he didn’t suggest anything, he would come in – especially on one of my solos – any way he wanted to.
Listening to that, he laid out a lot too, whenever Johnny was playing. That’s very rare, because – he was laying out a lot in those sessions.
Yeah. Johnny would say, “I got it. I got it. I got it.” You can hear him saying that on record – say it to Monk and me.
